subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow read-tool fallback for known binary document formats now, or wait for broader document parsing/provider-native file architecture?
rationale: The source-proven token-waste behavior remains, but the issue offers fallback versus parsing choices and related open issues cover wider document ingestion architecture.

options.title: Land Narrow Fallback
options.body: Guard known PDF/Office document reads in the read-tool path and return an actionable message while preserving normal text and image behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Document Architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as context for broader document extraction/provider-native file work and close or supersede conflicting guard PRs after that direction is chosen.

options.title: Route Parsing Outside Core
options.body: Keep core focused on the fallback and route rich parsing to a plugin, MCP, or ClawHub package unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Land Narrow Fallback
recommendation.body: Guard known PDF/Office document reads in the read-tool path and return an actionable message while preserving normal text and image behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main read-tool history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the immediate fallback decision.
